judged_text: The slug spread condition is inverted: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` writes slug only when billing is enabled, whereas the removed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` wrote it only when billing was disabled (the metadata/requestedSlug line kept its original polarity). On self-hosted deployments (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false) every new organization is created without a slug and is unreachable/unusable; on cloud the slug is now persisted before payment, bypassing the unpaid-state gating that the requestedSlug-in-metadata flow implements.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the spread for `slug` changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which reverses when `slug` is persisted. With `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED === false`, the new code will no longer include `slug` in the `organization.create` data at all, whereas previously it did. The `requestedSlug` metadata condition remains `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`-gated, so in the disabled-billing case neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` is written, making this a real behavioral regression introduced by the diff.
